chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Don Stovall and Courtney Williams at the Sunnyside Horseshoe
summary: Stovall took Willard Brown's place; Williams was a fine arranger and trumpeter.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well actually to go

back a little bit, it looks to me like Don Stovall took what's his name's place--took Willard Brown's place; not Buster, because Buster took his place. Buster shows up on these; Stovall came later, '42; Buster Smith took Stovall's place.
I think you've got that right.
Stovall must have come in--Stovall was working someplace out in Queens too with Sammy Price, I think.
He was working with me at a place called Sunnyside Horseshoe.
The Horseshoe Bar in Sunnyside?
Yeah.
He was a good saxophone player too.
Out of this world, but he didn't have much tone.
He had a heavy tone.
He had a heavy tone, but he wasn't as good as I liked them.
But he could play. Was he kind of a mean guy too?
I got along well with him.
He drank quite a bit too.
Yes. I got along well with most of the guys.
Courtney Williams was a nice arranger too, wasn't he?
Oh, he made a lot of stuff for me.
He was a good trumpet player too.
He was a fine trumpet player.
Is he still around?
Yeah, he's still around. A wonderful musician.
